meeting_header:
Date: 2027-03-22
Start: 14:30 UTC
End: 15:22 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Recording: yes
Attendees: Jamie Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Nguyen (Redwood SE), Maya Rao (CTO, Seabluff), David Klein (Head of Compliance), Priya Singh (Cloud Architect), Evan Ross (SRE)
summary: Seabluff is evaluating Redwood for a hybrid deployment — prefer Dedicated but need clarity on keystore residency, KMS routing, log sanitization for regulatory audits, and proof of audit evidence. They want a two-week pilot to validate latency and log-redaction before any procurement. Key concerns: key control, SSO/SAML mapping, masked logs for downstream analytics, legal hold, and cross-border logging retention.
topics: hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Jamie (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. We're gonna run through the residency and logging questions you sent. Carlos and I will try to hit SSO, KMS routing, and redaction.
[00:12] Maya (Seabluff): Hey thanks. Quick note — David from compliance is gonna mostly lead the questions. We're trying to avoid a full private deployment but we need guarantees.
[00:20] David (Seabluff): Yeah hi, hi. Short version — we can't have consumer PII leave EU. Also for some derivative outputs we need redaction and legal-hold proofs.
[00:32] Carlos (Redwood): Okay, understood. Do you currently use a cloud KMS per region?
[00:36] Priya (Seabluff): We use a mix — primary keys in Azure Key Vault eu-west, some in our on-prem HSM for the most sensitive wallets.
[00:44] Jamie: Right. So Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations. For Hosted we can accept a wrapped key — but the customer key material doesn't land in our control plane; we only see encrypted blobs, provided your KMS supports external-signing or key wrap. For Dedicated, you can bring your own key and we can pin instances to regions.
[01:05] Evan (Seabluff): When you say "pin instances to regions" — do you mean all tokenization and caches are also region-locked, or could telemetry leak to us-east?
[01:15] Carlos: Good question — by default telemetry and logs for Hosted cross-regions for ops, but for Dedicated we offer region-locked logging and we can configure log egress only to your VPC end-points. The control plane metadata still has some global indexes but we can pseudonymize them.
[01:33] David: Pseudonymize how? We need to show auditors that no raw PII ever left our jurisdiction.
[01:40] Carlos: There's a couple of layers — first we do request redaction at the ingestion layer, you can provide redaction rules (regex, named entity lists) that run before data is persisted to logs. Second, KV cache entries can be scrubbed — we can avoid writing raw prompts to persistent traces. Third, we support token-level masking in trace exports so only hashed IDs are present.
[02:05] Maya: That ingestion redaction — is it deterministic? We have complex account IDs that sometimes look like GUIDs, sometimes phone numbers.
[02:12] Carlos: It's rule-based plus optional ML scrubber. The rule layer is deterministic (regex or JSON path). The ML scrubber can catch fuzzy cases but we'll want a sample corpus to tune it.
[02:24] Priya: Would that ML scrubber run in your control plane or in our VPC?
[02:29] Jamie: For Hosted, the scrubber runs in our runtime; for Dedicated we can deploy the scrubber container into your VPC so all processing stays in your network.
[02:39] David: And for audit logs, we need append-only evidence with HMACs and a chain of custody. Do you provide signed audit bundles?
[02:47] Carlos: Yes — we can produce time-stamped, signed audit bundles for request/response hashes. For Dedicated we can integrate with your HSM to sign those bundles with your key. There's a slight lag (minutes) for bundle generation depending on throughput.
[02:59] Evan: About legal hold — if a subpoena requires requests from a date range, how do we show that we didn't drop the PII earlier?
[03:06] Carlos: Two options — maintain raw for legal-hold windows in a segregated encrypted store (we can limit access), or use cryptographic proofs (hash chains) that demonstrate the existence and non-modification of records while the content itself is redacted.
[03:22] David: I'd prefer the cryptographic proof approach because storing raw in any system is a liability for us.
[03:27] Jamie: Totally reasonable. We'll share a whitepaper on the audit-bundle format and the HMAC scheme.
[03:33] Maya: One more question on key residency: for multi-region failover, can Redwood route decryption to secondary keys that are also in the EU? We can't have keys in the US.
[03:44] Carlos: Yes, you can provision secondary keys in other EU regions and configure routing policies by latency and region. We do not require keys to be present in the US unless you opt in to cross-region failover.
[03:56] Priya: About logs retention — our policy is 30 days raw, 1 year aggregated, right now. We might want to keep only telemetry and hashed traces longer. Is that configurable per-tenant?
[04:07] Carlos: Yes per-tenant retention profiles are supported on Dedicated and Private. Hosted has fewer knobs. For Dedicated we can enforce retention policies and automatic purging, and provide retention proofs.
[04:18] Evan: Quick nit — will observability dashboards still show request traces with PII scrubbed or will they be blanked?
[04:25] Jamie: Dashboards show scrubbed/pseudonymized IDs; you can set role-based views so SRE sees aggregated latency/ token counts but not raw content.
[04:34] Maya: Can we map our SAML attributes to Redwood RBAC so our auditors can see who triggered requests?
[04:40] Carlos: Absolutely. We support SSO via SAML/OIDC and can map attributes to RBAC roles. For Dedicated you get SCIM sync as well.
[04:50] David: We're also concerned about model determinism and derivative data — if employees paste customer notes into prompts we need to ensure those snippets don't leak to other tenants or models used for fine-tuning.
[05:01] Jamie: We do not use customer prompts for model training. For Hosted we have a data use policy and opt-outs; for Dedicated and Private, your data never leaves your environment unless you explicitly share it.
[05:12] Maya: Ok that helps. On the pilot: we want a two-week test that validates 99th percentile latency under our throughput, plus a redaction efficacy run using 2k sample prompts. What would you need from us?
[05:26] Carlos: For the bench we'll need a sample traffic profile (qps, median/peak token length), authentication method (SAML/OAuth), example prompts (sanitized and raw as allowed), and redaction rules. We'll spin a Dedicated sandbox for you, route KMS to eu-west, and run both functional redaction and perf under your profile.
[05:42] Priya: Will the Dedicated sandbox be production-like? I don't want to skew results by weaker GPU types.
[05:48] Carlos: We'll match the instance types to the closest prod family. We'll document the GPU spec in the pilot runbook.
[05:55] Evan: Cost question — is the pilot metered or a time-boxed eval?
[05:59] Jamie: Typically time-boxed with usage metering so we can extrapolate. We'll give a provisional estimate for the pilot cost.
[06:05] David: A compliance question — can we get an independent pen-test report or attestation on the Dedicated environment?
[06:11] Carlos: We can provide our latest SOC2 and third-party penetration summary. For Dedicated we can also arrange tenant-targeted assessments under an MSA addendum, but that takes scheduling and budget.
[06:24] Maya: Who will be responsible for the redaction tuning? I assume some back and forth.
[06:29] Carlos: We'll do an initial tuning pass with your corpus, propose rule adjustments, and then you validate sample outputs. It's collaborative.
[06:36] Priya: About the scrubber running in our VPC — does it add latency?
[06:40] Carlos: Small overhead, usually single-digit milliseconds depending on rule complexity. We'll include that in the bench.
[06:47] Jamie: Quick callout — caching and prefix caches can reduce token cost, but you said many prompts are unique. How do you feel about prefix caching removal?
[06:56] Priya: Most are unique but conversation threads have repeated context. We'll test both.
[07:02] David: Last compliance ask — we need evidence for retention and deletion (proof an object was purged). Can Redwood provide verifiable deletion claims?
[07:11] Carlos: Yes — we can provide deletion receipts with signed timestamps and the underlying storage object's cryptographic nonce. For Dedicated you can have the signing key.
[07:20] Maya: Great. I think that's the bulk. Anything else?
[07:23] Jamie: I'll summarize and send artifacts. Carlos — anything on the technical checklist?
[07:28] Carlos: I'll draft the pilot runbook: region, GPU family, sample traffic, redaction rules, expected SLOs (99th p latency), and a success checklist.
[07:36] Evan: One random one — do you have a data minimization tool to strip user identifiers from analytics traces before we ship to our BI?
[07:44] Carlos: We can export aggregated metrics only, or run an additional redaction pass before export. We'll show options in the runbook.
[07:51] Maya: Ok let's cap it there. Thanks all.
[07:53] David: Thanks.
[07:55] Jamie: Recap: Jamie sends SOC2 and whitepaper; Carlos sends runbook and Dedicated pricing; Priya/Evan share redaction rules + sample prompts. Pilot week of 2027-04-04.
[08:07] Priya: I'll send a file with the redaction rules and a 2k prompt sample.
[08:12] Carlos: We'll follow up with a calendar invite for the pilot kickoff.
[08:18] Jamie: Thanks everyone, talk soon.
[52:00] (meeting end)
